title: The Germ Lab
story: You and NOVA are shut in a microbiology lab after a power cut. The doors open only when NOVA stops getting microorganisms wrong. Four locks stand between you and fresh air.
escaped: The lab doors hiss open. NOVA can now tell bacteria from viruses, check its own claims about medicines and spot a pattern in data.

locks.title: Fix NOVA's microbe groups
locks.intro: NOVA is learning the five groups of microorganisms. Some of its examples have the wrong group. Tick them.
locks.hint: Two of these are the ones you met in curd-making and in pond water. Which group does each really belong to?
locks.learn: If an AI learns from wrongly labelled examples, it repeats the mistakes with confidence. People who build AI spend a lot of time checking labels like these.

locks.title: Bacteria or virus?
locks.intro: NOVA must sort diseases by what causes them: bacteria or a virus. Choose the clues it should use, then test it on two new diseases.
locks.hint: Every one of these diseases has a vaccine, so that clue can't tell them apart. What works on bacteria but not on viruses?
locks.learn: A clue that is the same for everything (all have vaccines) gives an AI nothing to go on, and a clue like 'spreads through air' fits both groups. Antibiotics act on bacteria, not viruses: that real difference sorts them.

locks.title: Check NOVA's medicine advice
locks.intro: A classmate has a cold. NOVA has advice, and sounds sure. Is it right? Decide and pick the fact that settles it.
locks.claim: Take antibiotics: they will cure your cold and flu quickly.
evidence: Antibiotics are medicines that kill or stop the growth of disease-causing microorganisms.
Antibiotics are not effective against cold and flu, because these are caused by viruses.
Yeast is used to make bread rise.
Some antibiotics are made from bacteria and fungi.
locks.hint: What causes a cold? Does that kind of microorganism respond to antibiotics?
locks.learn: Half-true facts make AI answers sound convincing: antibiotics DO fight microorganisms, but not viruses. Checking the exact fact that tests the claim is what keeps you safe.

locks.title: How fast do bacteria grow?
locks.intro: Cooked food was left on a warm shelf. A lab counted the bacteria in a sample every hour. NOVA has to find the pattern.
locks.question: If the pattern carries on, about how many bacteria will there be after 4 hours?
locks.hint: Look at how the number changes each hour. Is it adding the same amount, or doubling?
locks.learn: AI finds patterns in data: here the count doubles every hour. That's why the textbook says to keep food cold or preserve it: microorganisms multiply fast in warm food.
